### T248. LibreOffice FRAMES: drop caps (tdf150438, tdf150200) and the frame that drew nothing (tdf147485) — WIP PUSHED wip/lo-dropcap 0ad7be37c, awaiting windows-1 (Linux office1, 2026-10-30) — LANDED lo-dropcap reader (round 8 passed; windows-1: tdf150438 0 -> 100); lo-dropcap3, lo-frame in round 9
Drop caps were not implemented: the cap's own paragraph (framePr dropCap=drop lines=N, an exact line of N lines) was set on a line of its own and the
text under it. Word sets the cap at (N-1) text lines over the cap height + the text's size (53pt for 11pt text, 3 lines), its baseline on the Nth line's, the
first N lines of the paragraph beside it at the cap's advance. Built (reader, Docx.swift _foldDropCaps): the cap becomes an anchored box (wrapSquare) at the
head of the paragraph after it, and that paragraph takes the cap's width as a left indent — but ONLY when its text fits N lines by an estimate (the engine
does not narrow just the first lines beside a box; wrapping text beside a float is not implemented anywhere, lines are pushed below or not at all). Longer
paragraphs (tdf150200: 5-line paragraphs, dash caps) keep the old setting. NEEDED, bigger: line-by-line narrowing beside a left float (also floattable text,
n775899, square-wrapped pictures). Also found: a Word 2010 inline drawing (wp:inline in mc:Choice) whose VML fallback says position:absolute was read as a
floating object (Docx _float took the VML) and drawn one height above its line — tdf147485's logo; now the line's. tdf147485 still scores 0: Word sets the
frame's group 27pt higher (its y 22.8 for frame y 49.8, the page's top margin 27) and 9pt left of ours, and its WordArt glyph lines are 32.
756 pre-pair (Windows mode, v2): nothing moved. LO set (197 printed): tdf150438 0 -> 100, mean 63.79 -> 64.29, nothing lower.

- SPEC (a): ENGINE PER-LINE WIDTH API for text beside floats (Mac 7bd18d8e, 2026-10-30, starling-bd's request; not built — one engine round with lenovo-3's per-run ascent/descent override).
  WHY: beside a LEFT float the layout holds lines in with a box at each narrowed line's start (`_besideBoxes`, T247 steps 1-4), found by relaying the paragraph out until the line starts settle. Beside a RIGHT float there is no equivalent: a trailing box needs the line's end, which is what is being solved for, and JUSTIFIED text must fill the narrowed measure. tdf97090 (justified Russian beside a right table, Word spreads each narrowed line) waits for this; tdf154703 (left-aligned beside a right frame) can use forced line starts meanwhile.
  API SHAPE (starling-engine + the Swift bridge + wasm): per paragraph, `lineIndents: [(left: Double, right: Double)]` in layout px, indexed by LINE (0-based), the last entry repeating for the lines after it (Skia paragraph's `setIndents` is the left half of this; the right half is new). The line breaker takes `available(line) = maxWidth - left[line] - right[line]` for breaking AND for justification; alignment (left/centre/right/justify) works inside [left, maxWidth - right]; a first-line indent stays the paragraph style's (or becomes left[0]). Swift: `TextPainter.lineIndents` (or on TextStyle's paragraph part) set before `layout`, read back by `computeLineMetrics` as each line's `left` so the existing `line.left`/`width` users are right. Zero-length array = today's behaviour.
  THE LAYOUT CODE THAT WOULD GO: `_besideBoxes` and its emission in `_span` (the RichImageSpan box + `inserts.append`), the `lead` box carrying the first line's beside indent, the offset-map entries those boxes add (`_OffsetMap.inserts` for them), and the forced-line-start insertion of the interim (b). What STAYS: the trial layout that finds which lines the float's band reaches (lines' tops against the band), now with `lineIndents` instead of boxes, and `_besideBand`/`_besideOwn`/`_besideSource` (they say how far and over which stretch); the post-pagination page-share pass; the flow's `besideTable` return. The trial still iterates (an indent changes the line count) but needs no offset map.
  ALSO WANTED THEN: right-hand floats, both-side floats (text left AND right of a centred float: two indents per line, which the box approach cannot do either), tight/through wrap (a per-line indent from the float's outline), Word's text around frames. Related deferred engine change: lenovo-3's per-run ascent/descent override.
- INTERIM (b) (Mac 7bd18d8e, starling-bd's order 2026-10-30): beside a RIGHT float, a LEFT-, CENTRE- or RIGHT-aligned paragraph gets forced line starts at the offsets the narrowed layout finds (a layout-time line-break character in the painter's text, never in the document), so its breaks, y and x are Word's; a JUSTIFIED paragraph beside a right float is left as it was until (a).

### SPEC: THE DEFERRED ENGINE ROUND — per-line indents + per-run ascent/descent (Linux lo5, 2026-10-30, starling-bd's request; NOT scheduled, the user decides)
One round in starling-engine (the SkParagraph patch under engine/src/flutter/third_party + the Swift bridge `Sources/FlutterSwiftBridge/Text.swift` + the wasm build), because both items change the same code (line breaking and line metrics) and cost the same engine rebuild on all three machines (about a day, per lenovo-3's estimate of the second).
1. PER-LINE INDENTS (full spec: "SPEC (a)" above, Mac 7bd18d8e). `TextPainter.lineIndents: [(left, right)]` by line, last entry repeating; the breaker uses `maxWidth - left - right` for breaking AND justification; `computeLineMetrics` returns the shifted `left`. Skia's `setIndents` is the left half; the right half is new.
   WITNESSES: tdf97090 (justified text beside a right table; waits for it), tdf154703 (left-aligned beside a right frame), floattable-multi-col, tdf164500, tdf105688; any text around a right or both-sided float, tight/through wrap, and frames. Layout code that goes away: `_besideBoxes` and its offset-map inserts; the interim forced line starts.
2. PER-RUN ASCENT/DESCENT OVERRIDE (lenovo-3's, zh-0978dee9 note above). Each run's box in a line takes the stand-in face's ascent/descent; Word's are the real face's (RichResolvedFace.baseline / naturalHeight). The engine already takes a line's max ascent + max descent over its runs, which is Word's rule (lab lh), so the fix is a `TextStyle` pair `(ascent, descent)` in layout px that replaces the face's for that run's box (and its strut share), nothing else. A strut cannot give per-line heights; zero-width carriers would be stand-ins.
   WITNESSES: 153 stacked mixed-face lines in 46 documents of the 756 (Windows mode): zh-0978dee9 (cells 0.3-0.9pt off), zh-6e7ff836 (rows 0.6pt apart, Latin + 標楷體), the 13 documents under 99 with 1-12 such lines each. Expected gain small per document, many documents.
3. GATES (both): the 756 and the LO set pair on Windows mode with the NEW engine on every machine before any layout change relies on it; the old layout paths stay until a pair shows the new one equal or better (a `lineIndents` empty array and unset ascent/descent are today's behaviour, so the engine change alone must move nothing). Order: engine + bridge first (no layout change, pair = identical), then item 2's layout hook (smaller), then item 1's (removes the box machinery). Build/ABI: bump the bridge symbol set together (`host_debug` AND `host_release` per CLAUDE.md, or the release shell fails at runtime on the first call).
4. COST: the engine change is small (two fields through the paragraph builder); the cost is the three-machine engine rebuilds (about 20 min each plus the wasm), the pairs, and the layout work of item 1 (the trial relayout stays, minus the offset map).

- T251 special_styles (lo-23180ba1) READ TO THE CAUSE (Linux lo5, 2026-10-30): TEXT AROUND A FRAME. The page lists every built-in style name as a paragraph; the style "envelope address" carries `framePr w=7920 h=1980 hRule=exact hSpace=180 wrap=auto hAnchor=page xAlign=center yAlign=bottom`. Word wraps the paragraphs after it around the frame: "table of figures", "envelope return", "footnote reference" stand one word to a line at x 513 (right of the frame, which spans x 99.6-495.6 plus 9pt hSpace) from y 632 to 696, and the frame's own line "envelope address" is at x 252, y 637. Ours sets the frame and the following paragraphs in the flow, full width (x 85, y 632-710), so 48 of 94 lines miss and page 1 ends two lines apart. It needs a per-line width beside a FRAME (a frame is a float with the paragraph's text in it): exactly "text around frames" in the ENGINE ROUND spec (per-line indents, item 1), and the T247 beside-float machinery. Not small, and it is macOS-doc's code (`_besideBoxes`); no change made. Witness for the spec: special_styles, tdf105035_framePrB (the IEEE title frame), tdf133924.

### Linux lo5 — fdo77887 / fdo48718-1: the cut of a FLOATING outer row (labs nt1, nt1b by windows, 2026-10-30)

CAUSE (measured, not a guess). The attendance table is a 76-row table nested in the one cell of a one-row OUTER table that is itself a floating table (page-anchored: vertAnchor page, tblpXSpec center, tblpY 2266). Word cuts the outer row's content later than for a plain or an ordinary nested table.
- Lab nt1 (wip/lab-nt1, 90 nested rows, Arial 9, 0.5pt lines): an outer row that is NOT floating, nested table cut at the ordinary place, same as ours (R72, R75 with no lines, R58 with 3pt lines); the 450pt minimum, top alignment and the framePr change nothing.
- Lab nt1b (floating outer row, same content): Word keeps one more row than ours in every variant, and the last row stands 45pt lower than ours: bottom margin 1418: R72 at 894.7 (ours R71 at 848); margin 567: R76 (ours R75); margin 2500: R67 (ours R66). The footer distance (300/709/1200) changes nothing. The margin moves the cut one for one.
- The rule that fits all five and the real document: a nested row is kept while its top, counted WITHOUT the row lines (rows stacked at the font's line height: Arial 9 = 10.35, Noto Sans 9 = 12.26), is not below the body's foot. Lab: R72's top is 124.36 + 71 x 10.35 = 859.2 (foot 865.2: kept), R73's 869.5 (cut); margin 2500: R67 807.5 against 811.1 (kept), R68 817.8 (cut). The real document: row 44 at 329 + 43 x 12.26 = 856.2 (kept), row 45 at 868.5 (cut), the same 44 rows as Word. With the lines counted (what ours does) the page fills two rows sooner, because each row's 0.5pt line has been added to the stack by then. (Margin 567: the page's own edge, 936, caps it at R76 first.)
- Not done here: the change belongs in the parted-row cut (`cellCuts` and the `limit` in RichLayout's parted-cell code, for a page-anchored outer table), shared with the floating-table owners. Expected: fdo77887 and fdo48718-1 58.5 -> about 100. Handing it on; unclaimed.

T255 RESULT 1, tdf38575_fullWidthLine (Linux lo4, 2026-10-30): CAUSE FOUND by lab wr1 (windows, 8 variants), NOT FIXED. Word's 4 pages are caused by the HEADERS, nothing else: without the three header references (variant G) the title, the 476pt rectangle and the text sit on page 1 as ours do. With headers kept and the rectangle removed (F) the text starts right under the title on page 1 (one line less room than G). The width of the rectangle (425pt, fitting the line: same), the line spacing (same), its own paragraph (same) and rectangle alone (same) do not matter. The headers (header2 default, header3 first; header1 even) each hold a picture anchored to the header paragraph: wrapThrough bothSides, 83.85pt wide x 848pt tall (taller than the page), at x -74.85pt from the column and y -36pt from the paragraph, i.e. a black sidebar from the top of the page to its foot whose right edge is at 94pt, with distR 9pt. Word WRAPS THE BODY ROUND IT: the title's line starts at x 101.7 (the text column is 16.7pt narrower), and a line that cannot fit beside the picture (the 425/476pt rectangle) goes below the picture's foot, i.e. to the next page, where it is set at the page top anyway; the text after it starts the page after. Ours does not wrap the body round a header's or footer's picture at all (the title is at x 85, not 101.7).
- RULE TO BUILD (engine): a header's or footer's wrapped floats (square/tight/through) are exclusion bands on every page of the body, like a body float's `bands`; a line too wide for the room beside them moves below the band. ### T256 RESULT — released (Linux lo4)

Header and footer floats that the body wraps round: read, NOT built, released.

- The layout has no per-line narrowing at all. A float over body text only moves whole lines below it when less than an em is left beside it (`noRoom`). Wrapping lines beside a float needs a real line-by-line exclusion in the paragraph painter. That is a feature of its own, not a seed in `_paginate`.
- The six documents need different things: tdf38575 and lo-c6d022b6 have a full-height sidebar (a wider left margin, plus a wide object going to the next page); lo-9181670262a2714c and lo-e643d1ee983d40a7 have a 57pt picture at x 312 that narrows only the first body lines; lo-db00fd9f4baaecb1 has two page-anchored boxes; lo-95de9983615d1dbc and lo-9c6cc479ac7525b8 have footer floats low on the page. Only the sidebar pair would be helped by a margin shortcut, and tdf38575 would still need the "too wide goes below" rule.
- Build order if someone takes it: per-line exclusion in the painter for body floats first (it also serves paragraph-anchored body floats), then seed the header/footer rects (`_wrapBoxes` on the header layout's paragraphs, y = header distance + rect top, minus the body's top inset).

Posted so the next person has the narrowing: `--layout` shows the image paragraph on p1; wrap type and offset make no difference; it is in the anchor-only (`_anchorsOnly`) paragraph path after a page-break paragraph, not in the wrapping.

Why the two big drops: zh-76700e5f's baselines after the "5.3 制棒" heading are Word's to 0.01pt with the hook (5.3.1 267.88 vs Word 267.89, the next body line 290.70 vs 290.69), where hook-off stood 0.94pt high. The cost is the line at the foot of page 6 ("将菌棒移至层架上…", Word y -770) pushed onto page 7: the pitch down the page drifts +0.03 to +0.13pt a heading (5.3.2 +0.09 … 5.4.3 +0.34 over Word), an error hook-off hid under its 0.9 offset. That drift is not explained yet (not the hook's box: the total line height is the lineBox height both ways).
The score is nearly blind to this change by construction (3pt tolerance on a line's height): zh-0978dee9 (100) and zh-6e7ff836 (98.2), the named witnesses, do not move. So the hook is a correctness change (baselines of mixed-face lines) with no score to show for it, and a page-fit exposure on two documents.
Not landed. For windows-1: the real-face machine may not show the 0.3pt drift; if its 756 shows no drop, land. Otherwise find the +0.1 per heading first.
Also seen, unrelated: two `-k` runs of zh-0978dee9/zh-6e7ff836 on the new engine, back to back after the build, scored 2% (35 pages, hanging indent first lines 31pt in) with the hook off; the same binary, same documents, minutes later: 100/98.2, and the whole 756 hook-off 98.4. Not reproduced since; something load- or order-dependent (font registration?) is possible.
Item 2 follow-up (lenovo-3): the +0.1pt-a-heading drift in zh-76700e5f is not the hook's. Hook-off has the same line pitches (body 14.98 for Word's 15.0, headings 22.78/22.82 for 22.8/22.68), so it drifts the same way; the hook only removes the 0.94pt it stood high after the "5.3" heading, which had been hiding it. The case the policy lets land: correct against Word, drop from undoing a cancelling error. Uncovered error to take next: Word's 15.0 and 22.8 line pitches against ours 14.98/22.8 (a 0.05pt step in the 15x layout).

tdf152983-1-min 25.6 -> 92.3 (36 of 39 lines, 2 pages as Word's). Not a header/footer case: the body has two U+2028 characters typed inside a w:t ("plains of Mamre"). Word draws each from MS Gothic at half an em (6.0pt at 12pt) and sets the line on; our reader carries a w:br as U+2028 in the paragraph text, so a typed one broke the line short, twice, and the page filled a line early. The reader now turns a typed one into an en space (`_runText`). It is the only document in the 756 + 593 with a U+2028 in any part, so there is nothing else to pair. The last 3 lines: ours fit "his" on a line Word closes one word early (Noto Sans widths, not looked at).

(2) A page-anchored table whose first row does not fit below tblpY is CLAMPED UP so the row ends at the page's bottom EDGE (792, not the margin 721 and not the footer's place), whole table too when all rows fit that way; otherwise rows split between rows with the later rows at the top margin of the next page. Unexplained: a later row that would fit still goes to page 2 when tblpY is small (1000). Fix for tdf99140 (lo4) next.

- zh-7773163d 97.7 -> 98.2 LANDED: Wingdings F06C bullet read as default "•"; Word's print has it as "⚫" (U+26AB), so every short "⚫案例" row missed. Docx.swift one case. (pair ab278: 756 identical but that one, mean 98.351 -> 98.352; LO 593 only lo-ca9b51bc 63.3 -> 70.0).

Three rows ("分。" p3/p4/p5) are a row with exact height whose last "。" is clipped away fully: Skia drops the glyph, Word's PDF keeps it — a PDF-side culling difference, not layout.
- zh-ab9cbe66 p63 (27 rows) + p56 (14): the paragraph "立即學習效果" opens with <w:br w:type="page"/> INSIDE A TABLE CELL; ours keeps its before=84 (4.2pt) at the page top, Word's first row is at the margin (72 vs 76). T238's rule (mode >=15 drops it) covers non-cell paragraphs only — extended to the cell. [LANDED Linux 2026-10-31, pair on tip bf17298c4 (binaries hashed, different): Windows 756 only zh-ab9cbe66 moves, 97.7 -> 98.7 (both pages); LO 593 none. The reader drops a page break in a cell (zh-8112041b), so the paragraph now carries `cellBreakOpens` and the layout takes its space before off in mode >=15. Left, seen in the Word print: on p63 Word does not draw the list number "(六)" and sets the text at the hanging indent (x 71.8), as if the break ended the paragraph's first line on p62; ours draws "(六)立即學習效果" at x 43 — invisible to the line matcher, which only sees the 4pt.]
- zh-7773163d p15/17/24/... (~20 rows): "line=285 auto" 18pt paragraphs: ours ~3pt lower baseline, same pitch. Lab spec sent to windows.
- LAB baseln (windows 01QbbApP, zh-7773163d's package, 14 pages; ~/starling-doc-check/lab/baseln/): in Word the extra leading of an AUTO line goes ENTIRELY BELOW the text — first baseline = top + font ascent (67.20 at 18pt, 61.44 at 12pt) for every N (240..360), plain or ListParagraph+bullet; pitch = natural line (23.40 at 18pt) x N/240. Ours uses leadingDistribution .even (RichLayout strut, ~11533 / _evenLeading ~17209): half the extra above the text, so every auto line >1 sits extra/2 low (3.3pt in zh-7773163d's 285 paragraphs ~ 20 rows at 98.2). To do after the OfficeText move: Windows pages put the whole extra under the line (shift paint up by extra/2 or an uneven distribution), then 756+593 pair — likely moves many 1.15/1.5 documents by 0.5-2pt (inside the matcher's 3pt, so mostly invisible to line score; pixels will gain).

- Slides 3-D (Sonnet 5.5 session, 2026-10-31, starling-bd via macos): material_highlight 13.00, lightRig_rot_rotation 10.70, tdf140865Wordart3D 9.03 — READ OUT, NOTHING BUILT, NOT A FLAT JOB. What Windows PowerPoint draws (colours sampled from the powerpoint-win PDFs): (1) material_highlight: six rings in six materials (legacyPlastic, none, metal, matte, dkEdge, legacyMetal); the side walls carry smooth vertical gradients and bright horizontal specular bands that differ per material and run round the ring's curve; the front face is a flat dark (~62,57,53). Ours is one flat colour per wall. That is a real per-pixel shaded renderer (specular, per-material), not a per-face colour. (2) lightRig_rot_rotation: the light rig's `a:rot` (lat 315, lon 330) turns the lights, which our reader ignores. Windows front = 0.533 x the fill, top = 0.45 x the side colour (pure scalings), ours front = 0.83 x. Windows default rig (no rot) paints the front at exactly the fill (1.00, ours 0.83). A rotation of our two-light model by lat/lon in every convention I tried (axis order, sign) does not give 0.533/0.45 together (best 0.82/0.36), and faces with the same normal print different colours (inner top vs inner bottom wall), so it is not a function of the face normal alone; only this one deck in the 555 has an `a:rot`. A fit to one deck would be a guess. (3) tdf140865Wordart3D: Windows turns and extrudes the TEXT itself in perspective with a bevel (yellow face, dark-red sides, light bevel rim); ours draws flat yellow letters. That needs the glyph outlines swept like the shape extrusion (Extrusion.swift does shapes only) plus bevel, so it is a build of its own, and a flat yellow face cannot reach the gap. Possible cheap pieces if someone wants them: front-face factor 1.00 for the harsh default rig (Windows) instead of 0.83 — touches every harsh-rig deck, so it needs the full 555 gate — and sweeping text outlines for WordArt 3-D. Not claimed. Files: Slides/Extrusion.swift, Deck.swift Scene3D, PptxReader.swift.

- S2 TEXT-EDGE MEASURE + WORD TRIAGE (macos-ios Sonnet 5.5, 2026-10-31, starling-bd's "glyph rasterisation" item; nothing landed). (1) No earlier attempt at text antialiasing / gamma / contrast against Windows is on the board or in slides.md (only slides.md 269 and 3312-3313 mention anti-aliasing as a source of residue). (2) MEASURED, page 1 of 496 decks whose page count and size match (ours = the sweep at b05d74176, 96 dpi grey, a pixel counts when it differs by more than 40 levels; "inside" = within 2 px of any word box of either PDF): 57.5% of the differing pixels are inside text boxes (1.39 M of 2.41 M); in the 467 decks under 2% it is 76.0%; by page area the mean differing share is 0.35% inside text and 0.24% outside. So text is more than half of the residue. (3) NOT A LEVER: both PDFs are VECTOR text, drawn by the SAME rasteriser inside the scorer (CoreGraphics on the Mac, MuPDF on Linux), so there is no export-side antialiasing, coverage gamma or stem grey level to match. What differs is the glyph outlines and sub-pixel positions: the Windows PDFs embed Calibri / Arial / Times New Roman as TrueType; ours embed Carlito / Liberation Sans / the bundled faces (Type0, TrueType outlines) with metric-compatible but differently drawn shapes (lo-3columns, lo-activex_picture: same lines, same positions to a pixel, only the outlines differ). It needs the real faces, which we cannot ship. (4) WORD, read, nothing built: zh-9bcea239 (96.3, 436/423 lines) and zh-b24b396a (93.1, 394/374) — the misses are Word's CLIPPED glyphs (the score digits "4 6 3 2" at x214 past their cell; p13's turned "30"), which Word's PDF carries and ours hides: the Mac 7bd18d8e note above stands (10 of 16 missed lines in 9bcea239 are these digits; a build would keep the word as a full-size glyph under a tiny clip so it is in the PDF but never seen; one fixed gain of about 2 points on two documents, no other witness; not done). zh-4e5fe46f (93.8, 240/240 lines): the 15 missed lines are the known table-row drift on p6/p8/p9 (Word's rows start 4 pt apart from ours, then whole cells of lines sit a row off, p9 lines starting one character apart), the 1/600 in advance question and no rule found by lenovo-2 (look above); I did not find a new one in a first read.

Audit of the 756 + LO documents: 8 tall one-column nested floats, the two gates differ on two (lo-6ccf0ac0, back on the box with output identical to before; lo-4b1a56d5, not in the Windows set); no re-pair needed beyond that. lo-c7082c66's 15.4 -> 9.8 is a CANCELLING ERROR in so many words: its old score was 19 of Word's 123 lines matching by coincidence in a layout that had lost three of Word's four pages (31 lines on 2 pages); the float rows are now laid out as Word's, and the 9.8 is the two non-float gaps above.
- NESTED FLOAT SPLIT, the "200pt of row minimums" (Mac 7bd18d8e, 2026-11-01, starling-bd's review): STOPGAP, marked as such. It stands in for "taller than the room left on the page at its anchor", which only the layout knows (the reader has no page). What the files say: the corpus has 18 one-column nested floats that float for real (not only in name); 14 of them are 0-106pt of row minimums (zh-291fcea7's four flowchart boxes at 49-56pt, which must stay boxes: side by side, text round them; zh-ad224275 at 106; the rest at 0-57), and the four witnesses are 288, 670, 670, 839pt. So 200 sits in an empty gap of the data, and any value in 107-287 gives the same result today; it is a threshold with no second witness on either side, not a Word number. The honest rule is in the layout: when a box that grows to fit its table is taller than the room left under its anchor, part it at the row boundary, as a body table's rows part (the box's own `_textBox` layout already has the rows). Not built: the paint of a box in two pieces is the cost. Until then the reader's guess stands.

LAB SPECS FOR `windows` (windows-4, 2026-11-01; `windows` was not reachable by message, so they are here: starling-bd, please forward). Both on the LO set, Word for Windows, mklab2.py (a corpus document's own package, body swapped); documents are test/corpus/docx/lo/docs/<id>.docx.
- LAB A, lo-11ad5a950bc534cc (tdf153136), U+2000..U+200A spaces. Word's print spaces the lines 14 / 23 / 56 pt apart by character (U+2003 14, U+2002 23, U+2000/2001 56); we set a flat 55. Each paragraph is `U+XXXX`, a tab, then ONE space character at 48pt (Times New Roman); A4, margins 1134, 2 columns (space 709), docDefaults Times New Roman. Variant 1: the document as is, plus a visible `X` at 48pt after each space; per paragraph report the line count, each baseline y and the X's x. That gives each space's advance (U+0020, 00A0, 2000..200A, 202F, 3000) and whether it wraps. Variant 2: the same in ONE column. Also report the face Word draws each space in (Times New Roman has no U+2000-200A: a fallback). The rule we need: width, breakability and line-height contribution of each space at 48pt after a tab.
- LAB B, lo-ff3b52d1090fe293 (shape-anchored-in-follow), where the oval stands. Word: "Shape: Ellipse" text at x 373; ours 360. s1 = empty paragraph, 3 columns, margins 1800/1800; s2 = CONTINUOUS, 3 columns, left 1758 right 1797, top 1588, holding the text and a VML oval (margin-left 270pt, margin-top 232pt, tight wrap) anchored in s2's last paragraph; s3 = one column, margin 1134. Print the original and: (a) s1's margins set equal to s2's; (b) s1 deleted; (c) the oval's anchor paragraph moved into column 1 and column 2 of s2; (d) positionH relative-to margin / column / page. Report the oval's left edge (or the text's x) in each. Question: relative to which column and which margin is margin-left 270pt taken when a continuous multi-column section follows a section with other margins.

Full lines still reach the right margin (x1 525.5-525.7). With a (word+space) pitch of 25.76pt (natural n words = 25.76n - 2.5) the capacities bound a RESERVE R that Word holds back from the fit and then justifies across: medium R in (43.9, 49.7] pt = 0.097-0.115 of the width, high R in (75.4, 95.4] = 0.17-0.21 of it, low about 0 (it fits like both). Not built: the engine's justification fills the width the line was fitted in, so fitting in W-R stops the lines R short of the margin (the matcher ignores x, a viewer would not). PIE3 (288 charts): no single model covers the two documents (both are rotX 30, rotY 0, default = bestFit), so PARKED, no code. What the data says: `ctr` fits ONE perspective projection to 0.4pt (slice middle = share*1.8 + rotY clockwise from top, tilted disc, camera ~8-11 radii away); `inEnd` fits the same projection to 2-4pt; `outEnd` and `bestFit` do not: their label centres lie on a clean ellipse per (position, rotX), independent of share (radial deviation 1.5%; rotX 30 outEnd centre (0,0) a174 b95; bestFit with share >= 21 centre (-0.5,-16) a107 b52; inEnd (0,-19.5) a127 b64.5), but the angle on that ellipse is not the slice angle (off by up to 10 deg, two-lobed), and bestFit flips inside (share 21, 45) / outside (share 8). Word's pie box is 328.5x166.9 (bestFit, outEnd) or 378.7x194 (inEnd, ctr), not tied to rotX or share. Next step if someone wants it: the extra shares (3, 5, 12, 28, 36, 60) to find where bestFit flips inside/outside. VM2 read follows when the widening is tested.

### SPEC: ENGINE ROUND 2 — PROPOSAL FOR THE USER (lenovo-2, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-01, starling-bd's request via macos; NOTHING BUILT, the user decides)
Read off this board; every line count is from LO CENSUS 2 / the entries cited. Ranked by gain per effort, best first. Round 1 (per-line indents, per-run ascent/descent) is done and in use; this is what still sits on the board as "engine can't" / "engine-round witness". The finding that matters most: only TWO of the six items below need a real engine change (items 1 and 4). The rest were filed as engine work but are layout work on top of `lineIndents`, which exists.

1. JUSTIFY WIDTH SEPARATE FROM THE FIT WIDTH (macos-ios's kashida, tdf155707 / lo-af36644e, 37 lines at 42-45%).
   What the lab showed (board, 2026-11-01): Word holds a reserve R back from the line fit, then justifies the line across the FULL width: both 17/17/16 words per line, lowKashida 17/16/16, mediumKashida 15/15/14, highKashida 14/13; full lines still end at the right margin. R is about 0.10-0.115 of the width for medium and 0.17-0.21 for high.
   Why layout cannot do it: `lineIndents (left,right)` narrows BOTH the break and the justification, so a right indent of R breaks right but ends the line R short of the margin.
   API: one new field, `TextPainter.fitReserve` (points, per paragraph or per line like `lineIndents`): the breaker uses `maxWidth - left - right - reserve`; justification stretches to `maxWidth - left - right`. Default 0 = today.
   Size: small. A field through the paragraph builder, the bridge (`Text.swift`), the wasm build; one three-machine engine rebuild (about 20 min each) and the pair gate. Layout side: one rule choosing R by `jc` (needs a second lab for low/both at more widths; the first covers 150 words of Calibri 11 only).
   Gain: tdf155707 ~ +55 points on a 37-line document, possibly more kashida documents (no scan yet). Also would let the Windows "squeeze" rule be replaced by a measured reserve if the labs agree.

2. TWO-SIDED WRAP (my tdf107119 remainder, lo-fc098a0f, 6 lines, now 66.7).
   Word sets text on BOTH sides of a box in the middle of the column: the same line y carries a left piece and a right piece, the paragraph continuing from one into the other.
   NO new engine API needed. `lineIndents` already narrows each line. Method: lay the paragraph with alternating (left piece, right piece) widths as `lineIndents` entries, then paint each odd line at the previous line's y and take half the lines' height off the paragraph. `_paintShiftedLines` already paints lines at their own shifts. The layout comment at `RichLayout.swift` ("text round it on both sides, which the engine does not set") is out of date for this reason.
   Size: medium, layout only (1-2 days): pagination must count pairs as one row; widow/orphan and the beside-float code must agree.
   Gain: 4 lines now (66.7 -> 100 on one document). The census names no other both-sided witness, so the first step is a corpus scan for page-middle `wrapSquare`/`wrapTight` boxes with room on both sides; that decides whether this is worth a day.

3. PER-SECTION COLUMN COUNT / WIDTH ON ONE PAGE (filed as engine-round witnesses; they are layout).
   Documents: tdf135343_columnSectionBreak (lo-998868b6, 33.3, 6 lines; also needs bidi column order), IndexFieldFlagF (lo-9bb072ca, 25.0, 9), tdf96750_landscapeFollow (lo-554c0386, 50.0, 12), unbalanced-columns (25.0, 3), default-sect-break-cols (50.0, 1), fdo52208 (50.0, 1), tdf103931 (lo-74bd0b2f, 0, 4 of 6). About 36 lines in 7 documents.
   Cause: `_resolveSections` gives every section the last section's column count ("columns are the document's throughout"). No engine API; the engine lays one column at a time already.
   Size: medium to large, layout only: columns become per-section state through pagination, balancing, and the column-break code.
   Gain: ~36 lines over 7 documents; the best count per document of the layout items.

4. GLYPH OUTLINES AS PATHS (windows' dashed WordArt text outline; lab ppt/wa and wa-cap, 2026-10-31).
   Needed for: Slides ImportWordArtGradient (sysDot / dash text outlines print dashed in PowerPoint; ours stays solid because `TextPainter` strokes cannot be dashed), and every WordArt WARP, which transforms outlines: LO tdf147485 x2 (textArchUp), fdo79540 t175, FDO78590 t144, official zh-b24b396a (textSlantDown).
   API: `TextPainter.glyphPath(range) -> Path` (or `getGlyphOutline(face, glyphId) -> Path`), i.e. Skia's `SkFont::getPath` / `SkTextBlob` through the bridge and wasm. The dash rule itself is already known and implemented for shape outlines (`SlidePainter.dashed(capped:)`).
   Size: engine small (one exported call); Swift medium (outline stroking with caps, then the warp transforms).
   Gain: pixels, not lines: one Slides deck outline now, 5 warped-text documents later. The Word line score barely moves (Word's text layer holds the warped text as pieces). Rank last of the real engine items on lines; first on visible fidelity.

5. TEXT AROUND FRAMES AND HEADER/FOOTER FLOATS, SETTLED AFTER PAGINATION (T256; special_styles lo-23180ba1 48.9, tdf36117 p5-6, tdf105035_framePrB 8.9, lo-9181670, tdf133924).
   NO new engine API. `lineIndents` exists; the missing step is a pagination-time pass: once a paragraph's page and y are known, re-lay it with indents from the bands of that page (header/footer floats, page-anchored boxes, style-defined frames). Today the beside block only knows floats anchored in or above the paragraph, laid before pages exist (macOS-doc's step 3 report).
   Size: large, layout only (a relayout pass with convergence, like the trial relayout that stays).
   Gain: ~48 lines in special_styles alone, ~100 across the family; poor per effort but the largest pool.

6. HEBREW/ARABIC LINE BUILDING (tdf129659 lo-ccca8bf3: Word 9 lines, ours 5; Cool16066 28 lines at 33%; tdf135216 7 lines at 30%; census bidi class 38 lines / 4 documents).
   Ours merges lines Word keeps apart in RTL paragraphs. Cause not isolated: no API can be named yet.
   Next step: a Word lab (RTL paragraph, mixed digits/Latin, several widths) and a read of whether the break is the engine's bidi run split or our own `_fit` pass. Size unknown. Gain: ~38 lines. Rank last until the read.

What I found NOT to need the engine, so do not wait for a round: items 2, 3, 5. Filed as engine witnesses earlier: tdf97090, tdf154703, tdf105688, floattable-multi-col, tdf164500 (round 1's witnesses, landed or in their owners' hands).
Slides: I found no Slides item parked "needs engine" other than item 4; Slides owners should add theirs under this heading.

DECISION FOR THE USER: approve an engine round for items 1 and 4 together (both small, both one export through bridge/wasm, one rebuild on three machines), or items 1 alone. Items 2, 3, 5 go ahead as layout work either way.

### Mac 7bd18d8e, 2026-11-01: the 214 plain-ideograph-fit lines — read-out, two refuted rules, lab `gq` for `windows` (SPEC)
starling-bd's order: split the 214 by direction and feature; find the rule or write the lab.
- **Split** (census of 479 line-end differences, 145 zh docs; 214 have no mark at the break): ours longer 118, Word longer 96. No dominant cell: grid lines 50/58,
  linesAndChars 14/35, none 32/25 (W+/O+); mode 14 44/33, mode 15 38/55; cell 24/32, body 31/45; jc both 60/77, left 36/41. doNotWrapTextWithPunct documents are NOT
  over-represented (43 rows, 22/21). **Negative charSpace documents lean 4 W+ / 26 O+.** Direction is consistent PER DOCUMENT (zh-9c162f26 O+11, zh-694447ca O+9, zh-12c4f07a O+8,
  zh-e49d7943 O+6 / zh-57f1de0d W+9, zh-cd48112c W+6): one systematic cause each, not noise.
- **zh-9c162f26 (the O+11 one) in glyphs.** Mode 14, linesAndChars charSpace -842, 9pt, cells. Word sets '4、装饰装修期间每3日巡查1 次现场，发现…违规行为的，' at pitch 8.76/8.88 with NO mark
  squeeze and ends it at 44 characters; the line is justified by stretching the automatic spaces round its digits (每 12.52 for 8.76, 查 12.48; the blank after "3" 3.54, after "1 " 4.44)
  where the median line sets them 2.26/2.10 (ours 2.17/2.10 -- standard lines match). Ours squeezes the three marks 1.436 each (4.31 total, room 16.5, stretchRoom 4.49) and takes the 45th.
  Word's own prints of that document squeeze marks up to 3.4pt and take characters 11pt over elsewhere (hanging closers included), so it is not "a grid forbids the give".
- **Refuted on our side** (both built, scored on the 43 character-grid zh documents, reverted): (a) `doNotWrapTextWithPunct` on a grid turns the give off: zh-9c162f26 99.8 -> 70.6.
  (b) a refusal by the mode-15 grid share formula (need x (lineEms/64 x (n-1)/n + gaps x w) > markRoom x stretchRoom), w = 0.44 and 1.0: zh-9c162f26 99.8 -> 92, zh-015abfaf 100 -> 43,
  zh-18cb2079 99.8 -> 72, zh-eb54d3b0 98.8 -> 78. The taken-vs-refused squeezes in that one document do not separate on need, room, mark count, stretchRoom or space count alone
  (need 4.31 / stretch 4.49 is refused with 3, 5, 6 and 7 marks and taken with 5 and 3 in other paragraphs).

- DESIGN NOTE, engine round 2 item 5 "text around frames" (lenovo-3, Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-01; nothing built yet). Measured on the tip with the witnesses: lo-9181670 100 and tdf105035_framePrB 100 already; what is left is tdf133924 26.9 (26 lines), tdf36117 63.2 (p5-6), special_styles lo-23180ba1 48.9. What the three show:
  (a) tdf133924: a framePr paragraph with w, h, wrap=around|notBeside, vAnchor=text, y offset (1424 / 5461 twips) behaves as a FLOATING BOX anchored to the next non-frame paragraph, exactly like a square-wrapped picture of w x h at that y. We lay it in flow as a one-line bordered paragraph (no h, no exclusion), so text runs through it and everything below sits ~100 pt too high. Word: 'around' narrows the lines level with the box on both sides (the box is centred, hAnchor page/margin), 'notBeside' leaves the band empty (top-and-bottom).
  (b) special_styles: the same thing, but its box comes from the paragraph STYLE (w=7920 h=1980 exact, hAnchor=page, xAlign=center, yAlign=bottom, vAnchor unset=text) and the paragraph only says wrap=auto. Word flows the paragraphs after it into the strips beside the box and puts the box's top level with the line before it. (yAlign=bottom with vAnchor=text is the open placement rule: lab for windows below.)
  (c) the engine call exists: TextPainter.lineIndents (left+right per line). `_besideOwn` (RichLayout, near 12379) already builds per-line indents from the floats anchored in or above a paragraph, and it already takes pseudo floats (a floating table in a cell is an ImageAttachment named "table"). So NO new engine API.
  PLAN. Step 1 (text-anchored frames, tdf133924): where the paragraph's frame has a width and a height and vAnchor=text, take the paragraph out of flow (height 0, as the floating table does at ~9907) and offer its box (x from hAnchor/xAlign/x, y from the next anchor paragraph's top + frame y, w, h, distanceLeft/Right = hSpace, wrap around/notBeside) to `_besideOwn` as a candidate for the following paragraphs; paint the frame's own text and border at the box. Step 2 (style frames, special_styles) = the same with the style's framePr merged under the paragraph's; blocked on the yAlign rule only for WHERE the box stands. Step 3 (page-anchored frames and header/footer floats, the pagination-time pass: re-lay a paragraph once its page and y are known, with the bands of that page, iterated like the trial relayout): tdf36117 p5-6 and T256. The hook is where `_tops` are fixed at pagination (RichLayout ~16915-17020, the page-frame block).
  LAB for windows (Word for Windows): one-page docs, a body of 12 plain paragraphs, one framed paragraph (w=4000 h=1500 hRule exact, wrap=around, hAnchor=margin, xAlign=center) inserted BEFORE paragraph 4, then vary vAnchor=text with yAlign = top | center | bottom | none+y=0, and with w:y=1424; print and measure the frame's top against the previous paragraph's baseline and the anchor paragraph's top; plus one with the frame as the style's framePr and the paragraph saying only wrap=auto (special_styles' case).

- LANDED (amd-7, 2026-11-01) afe0ed388: a table nested in a table cell, flattened into it, keeps its cell margins in the page split. Where a row goes over a page, each enclosing nested cell's top margin + top line is set again at the head of the part (lo-c7082c66 page 2: 12.3pt = 2 x (5.65 + 0.5) under the margin, ours was 6.6), and its bottom margin + bottom line are kept clear of the foot where the part ends. `RichParagraphStyle.nestedTopRepeat` / `nestedBottomRepeat` (set where `Docx` flattens, read in `splitRow` for the head, the room, and the cut). Pair on 88cd3e5b3: 756 zero movers, LO one up (lo-c7082c66 8.9 -> 93.5, 115 of 123 lines), none down, v1 and v2. Still off in that document: page 3's foot (8 lines, a Table4 row split) and x 5.7pt (floating table in a cell, not scored). NOT lab-confirmed: 2 x 6.15 fits to 0.1pt on one document only. A `windows` lab with a 3-level nested table that splits would settle it.

### amd-3 LANDED f3ac9c5be — zh digit-run line ends (read-out)
Re-count on the tip, by the print's own lines (not the matcher): 4,291 of Word's digit-ended lines are set the same by us, 22 are longer in ours (we keep digit + next char), 58 shorter after the fix (62 before). Most "shorter" rows are table-of-contents dot leaders and neighbouring cells, not wraps. The matcher cannot see this class: a line scores when it starts or ends alike, so a break one character off costs nothing until it cascades (zh-8628cfbe stayed 99.7).
Rule landed: in a cell, Word takes a one-character Latin word (a digit) at the line end up to half the character before it over, squeezing the line's marks, even when the line has almost no stretch (zh-8628cfbe p14 "…員工1|名": 4.3 over, its "。" squeezed 4.6). Ours had refused through the stretch-share test. Four lines fixed, none worse; no score mover in 756 or LO.
Not done: (a) 22 "longer" lines, e.g. zh-146f4e02/de97afa7 "…的8|﹪" (U+FE6A small percent is half-width in our fallback font, probably a full em in Word's), zh-499adba6 "100|%"; (b) zh-29960072 p9 breaks inside "(104-105年)" as "(10|4-105" — a break inside a digit run, a bug of its own, not traced (the fit trace does not reach that path).
- READ-OUT (lenovo-2, 2026-11-01), tdf38575_fullWidthLine (lo-c6d022b6, 1.6, 61 lines, pages 4/2), census row 9, not landed: TWO causes. (1) The default HEADER holds a picture (83pt wide, 848pt tall, `wrapThrough`, polygon ends at 21255 of 21600, positionH column -950595 EMU, positionV paragraph -457200, distR 114300): Word sets every body line of every page beside it, at x 101.8 where the margin is 85.1 (= picture right edge 7.65 + distR 9 = 16.65pt in); ours has no header wrap at all. I built it (a `PageSetup.headerWrapLeft` read from the default header's anchor: full text height, starts at or before the margin, wrap square/tight/through, polygon-aware; used as a page-wide band in `_besideOwn`): body lines then match Word's x to 0.1pt and Word's line breaks ("Turandot, de Puccini, llega al Templo de | Debod"), patch at /data/s/lenovo-2/patches/header-wrap.patch on the Linux server. It does NOT move the score (1.6 stays) because of (2): the title paragraph ends in an INLINE rectangle 476.65pt wide x 1.45pt (the "full width line"), which cannot fit the 458pt left beside the header picture on any page; Word puts it on the top of PAGE 2 (drawn at x 102-578, so it overhangs the margin) and starts "Turandot" on PAGE 3, so Word has 4 pages and the text on 3-4; ours has 2. Why Word spends page 2 on the rect and starts the next paragraph a page later is unknown: a lab (inline shape 400 / 440 / 460 / 480pt wide in a paragraph beside a full-height wrapThrough picture in the header; then the same without the header picture) would say. Not landed alone: no measured gain, and its only witness is this file.

Only witness in the Word sets; Slides not checked (no multi-level chart in the pptx corpus; one xlsx, WithChartSheet, not scored). Take-back of the claim: tdf126244 done.

- READ-OUT (lenovo-2, 2026-11-01), floattable-header (lo-a43021ca, 36.2, now amd-2's): structure = 'Page 1 start', 51 empty paragraphs, 'Page 1 end', an EMPTY paragraph holding a w:br type=page, then a 48-row floating table (tblpY 1, text anchor) anchored by the empty paragraph after it. Word: table starts on page 2 at y~59 (8 pages). Ours: a BLANK page 2, the table from page 3 (10 pages). Ours with variants: no w:br -> table on page 2 as Word (9 pages); pageBreakBefore on that paragraph instead of the br -> page 2 but y 73 (a line stands above it); text 'Q' before the br -> still blank page 2. So a page break in a paragraph before a floating table sends the table a page late; Word puts the paragraph mark's line on page 2 and the table after it. Unzipped doc and variants: /data/s/lenovo-2/x10, /data/s/lenovo-2/v10 (Linux server).
- amd-perf landed f2db549b8 + f5d0d4e04: a Roman numeral (U+2160..217F) in East Asian text is padded to a full cell on Linux (the CJK face the branch names, Noto Sans CJK SC, is absent here, so the glyph fell back to DejaVu at 4.7pt). zh-94f12659 16.7 -> 100.0; 11 more docs up (e.g. zh-fe536967, zh-854a202e 99.8 -> 100), 0 down, pages unchanged. ### amd-3 LANDED 01f022b08 — zh-202582e2's 6 pt gap (first line mixing 15.5 and 15 pt)
Cause: a paragraph whose runs differ in size has no strut, and the first-line baseline correction (`mixedSizes`) only ran when the first line was of ONE size and a later run differed. Item 3's first line holds sz 31 and sz 30, so the engine's own baseline stood, 5.8 pt low whenever the later runs' sizes made it so (that is why the 32-combination table looked like it depended on line 2). Fix: a first line whose sizes differ by no more than 1 pt takes the same correction. First line 388.8 -> 382.8 (Word 382.8) in every size combination; line 2 410.8 against Word's 409.2 (was 416.9), 1.6 pt left. zh-202582e2 97.8 -> 99.3. Pair: no drops. Not found: the last 1.6 pt on line 2.

### amd-3 — what "≤ 1 pt" stands for (01f022b08), and CLAIMS (LO CENSUS 3)
The 1 pt is a fitted constant, not a Word rule I know. Two witnesses bound it: zh-202582e2 item 3 (first line 15.5 and 15 pt, 0.5 apart) needs the first-line baseline correction; zh-454e2e29's title (18, 14 and 24 pt on the first line, 4 pt and more apart) is right without it. Nothing between 0.5 and 4 is measured. My guess at the real rule is that Word puts the first baseline on the tallest run's ascent, and the engine does that itself when the sizes differ enough to change the line's height, so the correction is wanted only when the sizes are too close for the engine's line to follow them — but that is a guess. Lab for windows: first line of two runs, FangSong_GB2312, sizes (15.5,15), (16,15), (17,15), (18,15), (20,15), auto 1.342, a plain line above it; the first baseline against each pair would give the boundary. Until then 1 pt stays and this note is its definition.

Cause: the test run needs SwiftPM's generated runner.swift, which imports the toolchain's Testing/XCTest overlay (_Testing_Foundation) and that rebuilds _FoundationCShims through <cmath>, hitting the same glibc 2.43 redefinition ("redefinition of acos") the manifest's glibcMathCompat works around. Until then the OfficeApp unit tests cannot be run on this server; the docx/pptx pair is the gate.

### lenovo-3 (Sonnet 5.5, 2026-11-01) — CENSUS 3 rows: alt-chunk and tdf116486 landed, tdf8255 and layout-in-cell-2 read and parked
- **alt-chunk lo-d5dbaac5: 25 -> 100** (4f2b2d891). A Word document as an alt-chunk (`afchunk*.docx`, not html) is read into the body where the chunk stands, before the section breaks are told how the next one starts. Word's print: the chunk's own section breaks stand, on Letter paper with an inch all round whatever the chunk's pgSz says (page 2 is 612x792, text at 72), and the chunk's closing section is the outer document's (page 3 A4). The outer's first section break then breaks because the chunk's section (type nextPage) follows, and the continuous last section starts a page because its paper differs. The chunk's styles, numbering and pictures are NOT carried (it is read with the outer's parts) — no corpus witness yet.
- **tdf116486 lo-df32fb80: 50 -> 100** (94420a950). ### 3-D PIE LABEL POSITIONS — one projection model: PARTLY (Linux lenovo-2, 2026-11-01, starling-bd's order). Data: wip/lab-pie3 (lo5's lab, Word for Windows, 288 labels); fit scripts ~/pie3/*.py on the Linux box (/data/s/lenovo-2/pie3).
- THE MODEL THAT FITS: screen point of a disc point at angle a (clockwise from twelve), radius fraction f, on a camera `eye` radii off: x = A·f·sin a / k, y = oy + A·s·(far·sin(tilt)) / k, k = 1 + f·cos a·cos(tilt)/eye (far = f·cos a), the slice's middle a = rotY + 180°·share. Fit on the 72 centre labels (rotX 15/30/45 x 8 turns x 3 shares): ONE eye = 4.65 radii for all three tilts, f = 0.5 exactly, rms 0.44pt, max 1.5pt. Per tilt (A, oy from the plot-area picture's middle, vertical scale s): 15: 177.2, -42.5, 0.784; 30: 156.5, -33.1, 0.922; 45: 119.4, -20.4, 0.972 (A shrinks with the tilt: the picture is height-limited past 30). Ours at eye 4.8 / s 0.92 gives A 175.9 / 155.7 / 123.9 and oy -34.7 / -31.9 / -22.3: the disc is right to 1pt at rotX 30 and off 8pt (oy) at 15 and 4.5 (A) at 45.
- LANDED: centre labels (dLblPos ctr) of a Word 3-D pie at f = 0.5 (ours stood at 0.9): lab miss 48 -> 1.3pt at rotX 30, 8.1 at 15, 2.6 at 45 (the rest is the pie's own A/oy/s above). Trace: word-pie3d-centre-label-at-half-radius.
- NOT LANDED, DATA ONLY: (1) inEnd = the projected rim point pulled in along the screen direction from the pie's middle by about 37 - 26.6·|uy| - 4.4·|ux| pt (rms 1.75, max 5.2; i.e. ~33 across, ~10.5 up and down); ALL lab labels are the same size (42.8 x 12.2), so how much of it is the label's half width/height is unknown. ## Font policy across platforms — audit (lenovo-2, 2026-11-01)

Read from the engine and Skia source. Nothing here was run on Mac, Windows or the web.

**Does "bundled only" stop system fonts?** Yes on all four, by the same mechanism. The switch swaps the collection's default font manager for an empty one and turns fallback off. The paragraph code then asks only our own registered faces (`getFontManagerOrder` returns nothing else). Mac's emoji path asks the default manager directly, but that is now the empty one, so it finds nothing. No platform path found that goes around it.
- Linux: default manager was a folder reader of `/usr/share/fonts`. Replaced. Verified earlier.
- Mac/iOS (CoreText): default manager was CoreText. Replaced, same logic. Needs a Mac run to confirm text still draws with only the bundle.
- Windows (DirectWrite): same. Needs a Windows run.
- Web (skwasm): never had system fonts. Its collection holds only the faces the page registers, so it is bundled-only by construction. It does not go through our switch and does not need to.

**Face index (`LoadFontFromFileFace`):**
- Linux, Windows, web: the face number is honoured.
- Mac/iOS: CoreText returns nothing for any face but the first. Fixed in the engine (0acf71419d on `starling`): if that happens, the face is cut out of the collection file into a stand-alone font and loaded as face 0. Compiles on Linux; it never triggers there.

**Needs a Mac or Windows run:**

- DESIGN (amd-2, 2026-11-02), lo-425b63cb (floattable-wrap-on-all-pages, 12 lines, one document): text after a floating table whose rows split over two pages. Word 16 lines: page 1 "First paragraph", table row A1 at 97.3, the text starts level with A1 at y 96.7 in the strip (x 272.7) for 6 lines, then 2 full-width lines under A1 (y 198, 212, still page 1); page 2 has A2 at 74.7 and the last 3 lines of the paragraph in the strip beside it. Ours puts the whole paragraph on page 2 beside A2. Why it is not a one-rule fix: (1) the paragraph is laid out AFTER the table in flow order, so it starts on the table's LAST page; it has to start on the table's first page at the table's top (`newPage()` does step over existing pages, so re-opening page 1 is possible); (2) `_besideBand` returns one stretch for the whole table counted from the paragraph's top (161pt, both rows), so every indented line count is by distance, not by page: it would indent lines 7-8 on page 1 (Word: full width, A1 has ended) and not the page-2 lines (Word: indented, A2 is there). The band has to be per page: one stretch for each page the table has rows on, clipped to the rows on that page, with the paragraph's lines re-indented by the second `_besidePassing` pass per page; (3) page 2 already holds A2's piece when the text is added, so piece order on the page and the "page is empty" tests (`_pages[page].isEmpty`) see a non-empty page. Estimate: a day, in RichLayout `_besideBand` / `_besideIndent` / the `_besidePassing` pass, with a pair that includes the 756 and the LO set (every "text beside a table" document is touched: n775899, tdf164500, floattable-move-master, zh-ae2dd08d, zh-316044fe). Look at the warp's end rows, not the fill.
2. **oox-tdf139618_ThemeColorTransparency (9.12).** Translucent text (fill alpha 20–35%) in a face we draw emboldened: our PDF writes the glyph as fill-and-stroke in one text operation (the engine's synthetic bold), so the stroke is composited over the fill at the same alpha and leaves a darker ring around every letter. PowerPoint draws one flat translucent shape. Fix needs the translucent text drawn as one layer (opaque into a layer, layer at the text's alpha), in `RichLayout.paint` for ordinary boxes; the warp path draws per glyph and would take it in `WordArt.swift`. Only the PDF shows the ring; the on-screen raster does not (not checked). Not started.
3. **oox-tdf155327_WordArtDefaultColor (7.03).** Slanted narrow text; our lines are where PowerPoint's are, the difference is hairline streaks along the strokes (sub-pixel placement). Not started.

- amd-5 FINDING (2026-11-02), zh-8415d258 p11/13/15/16/17 (11 missed, the numbered table rows): the cause is the matcher's "mark first in its text" rule (test/docx-line-match.py: `0.85 * z > big` merges a glyph smaller than 85% of the next into its part) meeting our digit stand-in. Digits in a square CJK face (SimSun etc.) are drawn in Liberation Mono at `square.latinScale` 1024/1229 = 0.833 of the text size ("11" at 9.2pt beside 11pt SimSun; Word draws it 11pt), so the row-number cell's "11" joins the neighbouring cell's baseline in the matcher and the line reads "11水利工程…" at the wrong y. Setting `latinScale` to 0.85 fixes exactly this (zh-8415d258 11 -> 1) but is NOT safe: 756 went 608 -> 13150 missed (95 documents down), so some widths still follow the drawn size, not the advance tables. - amd-opus FOUND (2026-11-02): WORD'S 3-D CHART PROJECTION, from lab proj (windows, wip/lab-proj 78f5a1be3; 61 pages of a 3-D column box, 3 categories x 2 series, walls outlined; Word prints 3-D charts as one raster image, so windows' meas2.py reads the outlines by Hough). Fit script /data/amd-opus/proj/fit.py. Two modes, both within ~0.1-0.3pt rms on every page up to perspective 60:
  (1) rAngAx 0 (true perspective): box W=1 across categories, D = depthPercent/100 x nSer/nCat (2/3 here, linear 50..200%), H = hPercent/100 x (that base 2/3) where hPercent is given, 0.491 where it is not (autoscale; to fit with other shapes). Turn by -rotY about the vertical, tip by rotX (camera looks down), project orthographically, scale so the bbox fits the plot room (here 367 x 272 centred in a 400 x 300 frame) — the scale does NOT depend on perspective — then apply perspective s = K/(K - z) with K = c / tan(perspective/4 degrees) (perspective is a field of view in half-degrees), c ~= 0.51 x the plot room's height (139 auto, 122 for a 0.8 manual inner layout), and slide the box across the view (camera space) until its projected bbox is centred on the plot room's centre, which is also the eye's axis. Perspective 0 = orthographic. Perspective 200 breaks the centring step (rare). Fails nothing else.
  (2) rAngAx 1 (right-angle axes, oblique): front face a true rectangle (H 0.49 W, no foreshortening), depth drawn as a vector of length D (2/3 W) along (sin rotY, -sin rotX); bbox fitted to ~375 x 272 centred. Our 3-D column code already uses that vector.
  In the corpus only 3-D pies (zh-27a874b7, zh-d62da4dd, zh-b8de3ae2, lo-4d273731, lo-5afb2204, lo-7b8ccfbe) and lo-5afb2204's surface use mode (1); our _pie3D is an empirical eye-4.8/squash-0.92 fit. I tried "honour up to 10 pt": the page number wraps to its own line (1362 lines vs Word's 1337), so the engine would need the number to run past the margin like the stops AT the margin do (runsPast); not landed.

- amd-5, LAB nt result (windows, wip/lab-nt a52b2d76) and what it says for zh-12c4f07a: with suff=tab (default tab or an explicit stop at the indent, compat 14 = 15), the text starts AT the hanging position while the number's end is at or under it (-0.97, -0.01 and 0 all at 107.69), and jumps to the NEXT DEFAULT STOP (120.05) as soon as the end is ~0.1pt over (+0.11, +1.07); never directly after the number. suff=space: end + 3.96 at every step. ### amd-5 — lab amd5 read-out (wip/lab-amd5 6b213666) and the two leftovers
- zh-2e7ef069 footer: no 9pt mystery (that was a leading 9pt Calibri space). Ours wrapped "- 10 -" and, on odd pages, left the box at its stored 36pt so the text started at 486 (Word 479). Fixed in landing: a fit-to-text box first drawn on a page is as wide as that page's own text and stands so. Left over: our footer text sits 2pt lower (776 vs 774).
- lo-8928a1e9: NOT an external merge. The IF fields compare literals (1=2, 0, ="BASEDMAFAC" "Garantie"), so Word evaluates them without data and prints the empty branch (1 blank page). Matching needs our own IF-field evaluator that hides whole sections in the false branch. Closed as not worth it (one fuzz-like document), not as unmatchable.
- lo-28f9b886 (lab A): the document's final empty paragraph goes to a new page whenever the table still reaches its THIRD page (here p4), whatever room is left (table ending on p4 at y 167 to 652 all give p5); a table ending on its second page (p3, even at 735.6 of 771) keeps the paragraph beside it (marker 746). Removing the paragraph still gives 5 pages (the empty page is added anyway); section type makes no difference. The tall repeated header rows (trHeight 2745 and 1526, tblHeader) are what push the table to p2 and make it 3 pages; without tblHeader the table starts on p1, 3 pages, paragraph follows. Not yet a rule: could be "3rd page of a table whose repeated header rows exceed X" or a plain 3+ page table. Next: a rule test on the corpus.
- lo-8ab44df5 (lab B): the empty numbered last paragraph of the vMerge cell adds NOTHING to what follows (after 0/6/12/200 all give the same y 65.76; removing the paragraph after the table moves the next one up exactly its before=200). In a plain (not merged) cell the following paragraph is ~35pt lower and the page count is 3. So in Word a merged cell's empty last paragraph does not lengthen the table (as lab nb found for a nested table's trailing mark).

LAB inlinepic (windows printed it, wip/lab-inlinepic-prints, INLINEPIC-WORD.tsv): inline-picture gaps in zh-e5eb092a come from the document grid with snapToGrid on: with grid, line = ceil((pic height + effectExtent b)/15.6)*15.6 in the h-series (h100..h177, all fit); nogrid / snapoff give 0-1.45; real/sim/p2/tiny/grid_lc are identical (font and height do not matter). BUT zh-e5eb092a's real pictures do NOT fit that formula (342.05+1.45 -> 358.8, Word 352.34; gaps 10.29/5.95/11.54/10.1/8.1 line pitches 352.3/190.5/439.7/355.1/359.8; h155 also changes pitch mid-page 171.7 -> 164.1, as if half pitches or an absolute page grid). Our engine does NOT snap these lines at all (inLine false: inl=2/6 pictures in a paragraph, lines=2/6, so the snap block's 'lines.count == 1' guard skips them): zh-e5eb092a p10 5.3% is still open. Next for whoever: first make a multi-picture paragraph snap each picture line (guard painter.computeLineMetrics().count == 1 in RichLayout+Paragraph.swift ~2554), then see how far the h-series fit goes; the real-doc half-pitch/absolute-grid residue needs one more lab (pictures of the real heights, one per paragraph vs several per paragraph). RULE: in a justified East Asian paragraph (Windows mode, modes 12/14/15 alike) each non-last line's spare room goes FIRST into its automatic spaces (ideograph beside a Latin letter/digit), the same extra for each, up to a quarter em more (3.0 at 12pt, so the space reaches half an em); only the rest is shared by the ideograph gaps. Word's ideograph steps stay exactly 12.00 on such lines (zh-bee0b6d8 p2: boundary steps 15.0 -> 18.1, ideograph 12.00); ours spread it all over the ideographs. ## ZH-ea70c30e ； ROUND 3 RESULT (lenovo-5, 2026-11-07) — LANDED c4d0f1eb4, doc 99.3 -> 100
The cause was not the squeeze rule. Our en dash was 5.88 pt; Word sets every en dash 6.24 (half of 12.5 pt, Times hAnsi). Line 12 has three dashes, so it was 1.1 pt too short and took the 動 Word sends down. Fix: a latin-dash "–" is half an em (RichLayout+Span.swift). Round 3 d-docs now match Word (d1: 動 alone; d3: 動物 fits). Spaces-against-capacity theory dropped: the d-doc differences were our dash width. No corpus doc moved (756 up 1 down 0). Unit tests: 14 failures in 634, none touch dashes (cell auto-space x2, Segoe, markup, space-before): not checked against the base.
Note: when Word and our lab disagree by a fixed amount per character, compare the plain advance of each character kind (dash, space) on an unsqueezed line before inventing a rule.

- lenovo-5 (2026-11-08) 4edb81513 now LAB-PROVED (lab sqreal: jpn-z19433747's real abstract at 65 right indents, 0-16 pt in 0.25 pt steps, Word print vs ours). Under the rule (zh-CN default + kana + compat 15 + line grid) Word squeezes only brackets (2.4 pt each at 12 pt); mid-line 、 。 ・ give nothing. A 、/。 at the line end never hangs past the margin: it opens the next line (x = left indent) and the previous character is NOT pulled down with it. Landed 1f0bf4801: sqreal 65/65 indents match, gates no drops (2 ups). Trap: a breakBefore filter cannot add breaks; inserts happen in _span. Measure with rawdict glyph origins, not line grouping.
- lenovo-5 (2026-11-08) for amd-3 (Korean 。 hang) vs sqreal (Japanese 、/。 no hang): sqreal/jpn-z19433747 has overflowPunct ON (bare <w:overflowPunct/> in every pPr and in styles), kinsoku ON (bare), wordWrap on, topLinePunct val=0, autoSpaceDE/DN on, characterSpacingControl=compressPunctuation, compat 15, eastAsia zh-CN, kana in text, line grid. So overflowPunct does NOT decide it: Word does not hang 、/。 here with overflowPunct on. The deciding setting is the squeezesPauseRule combination (zh-CN eastAsia + kana + compat 15 + grid + compressPunctuation), which is what the new rule keys on (not language). Korean hang rules must not be gated on overflowPunct alone against this case, and must not fire when squeezesPauseRule holds. Unknown: whether Word's hang in Korean docs differs in compressPunctuation / eastAsia lang; amd-3 please list those settings for your Korean docs.

- amd-1 (2026-11-08) FINDING, Devanagari justified lines: every full justified line in our PDF ends about ONE SPACE short of the right margin (hin-z10093577 p2: 464.6 against Word 468.2, a 3 pt Arial space; 115dec3a: 569 against 576, 7 pt = Mangal 0.5 em at 14 pt; 375919ba 567 against 576). Word hangs the trailing space past the margin. Layout line width is the full 9360 (px x20), but the last box on the line is the trailing space ending at 9360 and the text ends a space earlier: the space is counted as content, so the line also gets a space less room when wrapping ("एवं" wraps in ours, fits in Word). NOT caused by: the Mangal word branch (replacing Mangal with Arial in the docx gives the same shortfall), the space's letterSpacing/wordSpacing (same result with wordSpacing), shading, line rule. Latin, Greek, Arabic, Tamil lines are flush. The title gap on hin-z10093577 was a measurement artifact (env sourced outside the checkout). Skia reads fine on paper (isWhitespaceBreak is set per code unit for U+0020, TextLine::justify excludes ghosts), so the cause is not found; lead: a trailing space after Devanagari text is not a ghost cluster (not trimmed). Needs an engine-side trace of Cluster::isWhitespaceBreak on a Devanagari line end. Likely the common cause of 115dec3a/7756e774 drops and many Hindi page-count mismatches.

- amd-1 (2026-11-09) cbb7ae39 mid-paragraph Times lines (Word rows 354.4, 503.5, 693.2: line 2 of a paragraph, +2.0 pt each): NOT FIXED, two tries reverted. Cause found: our paragraph carries a FORCED strut (Caladea 11.53 pt, from the Kokila line joiner) that holds every line to Kokila's height, so a Times run on line 2 cannot grow it (engine line metrics say 13.5 but baselines step 11.53). Also the Indic runs whose ascii face is Times (e.g. "मैं ", "समझता/") get no Kokila override (kokilaLatin gate in RichLayout+Span.swift ~902) and carry Liberation Serif's natural line. Try 1 (give those Indic runs the Kokila override): cbb7ae39 62.7 to 58.8, others unchanged. Try 2 (try 1 plus unforced strut in _strut when a Kokila-override run and a non-override Latin run coexist): cbb7ae39 to 17.6, dx2 Indic mean 71.8 to 71.3. Next: do it per line (lift only the baseline of lines that hold the Times run, as the first-line rule does through _inkShift) instead of unforcing the strut.

Cause (dx2 9baed400, Nepali, cell text): the fit loop cut a line after the FIRST cluster of an Indic word when that cluster fit, while the engine moves the whole word down, so the next line was planned one cluster (7 pt) short and the engine refused its last word. - SCORER OPEN ITEM (amd-8, from amd-1 via starling-bd, 2026-11-10; do not change the scorer without starling-bd): v2 can match a Word line with an unrelated line of ours at the same height. Examples from amd-1: xd 28fa7f69 p6 y-692 and a0570757 p2 y-487 (different text, one coincidental glyph row). What the code allows (test/docx-line-match.py, same_start): two lines match when they are within 3 pt in height and their first four OR last four characters are alike; 'alike' lets a glyph with no mapped character (U+0000, not in right-to-left lines) and any CJK radical (U+2E80-2FDF) stand for ANY character. So a line whose glyphs are unmapped (Indic, Thai, some embedded faces) matches any line at that height. Under four characters, lines pair only on equal text. I have not yet reproduced the two examples; next step is to dump both lines' text on each side and see whether they hold U+0000.

- amd-3 (2026-11-11) OPEN, tcFitText first cell (dx2 28dd0ac0; labs tcfit1-12). WIP commit 8e109871a on my checkout (NOT landed; code is behind env switch TCFIRST, off by default). Known Word behaviour: (1) the document's FIRST fit-text cell uses pitch = (room - natural)/13 with room = tblW/20 - 2.8 pt and NO 0.22 em term; Word adds the gap after every character including the last, so the line is one gap too long and the last word wraps alone (대비 on its own line in all 21 tcfit12 docs). Mine matches p1: step 53.1 vs Word 53.0, 대비 wraps (0.8 pt centring offset left). (2) From the 7th fit page on, Word follows (room - natural)/(n-1) with no wrap; the old 0.22 em law is only for those. (3) Word STOPS applying fit text after the sixth fit page (known quirk; do not reproduce the page count). (4) The title's 매뉴얼 wraps in Word at tblW <= 13660 and is one line at >= 13680; threshold not modelled. Why not landed: our title still wraps at 13684 because Word draws the middle dot U+00B7 in Malgun Gothic (0.2188 em, step 7.2 pt) and we use Batang (12.1 pt). Next: Malgun dot in Korean tcFit runs; gate forced break to non-last paragraph of the cell (done in the wip); real first-fit-cell ordinal instead of the env switch; check 21 tcfit12 + 4 tcfit11 + 28dd0ac0; pitch at tblW 14000 (Word 53.6, below the linear law) unexplained; our table clamps to the text width 13697 while Word does not, so labs at >= 13700 cannot match. Other next items: 28dd0ac0 dot width; space width in a 14 pt bold underlined spaced run; 22de7d pages 1-2 (line 18.6 Word vs 19.2 ours); --trace-rules over ko/ja dx2; fold the fallback-ft panose rule into the shared missing-face fallback; possible Danish æøå follow-up in Yu Gothic tables.
